Q Text: You are given an unsorted list of positive and negative integers. You must determine if there exists a pair of values (a, b) such that a + b = 0. Which of the following approaches has the smallest (most efficient) time complexity? Assume that no index has the value 0.
Answer: Sort the list. Then, iterate through the list and for each value a perform a binary search to check if the value (a * -1)  is present in the list. If (a * -1) is found, then the pair exists, but if we check all possible a values and do not find (a * -1) then there is no pair.

Q Text: You are given an unsorted list of positive and negative integers. You must determine if there exists a pair of values (a, b) such that a + b = 0. Which of the following approaches has the smallest (most efficient) time complexity? Assume that no index has the value 0.

If not, then add value a to the Hashset if it is not already present. If we check all possible a values without finding the pair then there is no pair.

Q Text: You are given an unsorted list of positive and negative integers. You must determine if there exists a pair of values (a, b) such that a + b = 0. Which of the following approaches has the smallest (most efficient) time complexity? Assume that no index has the value 0.
Answer: Sort the list. Then, iterate through the list and for each value a perform a binary search to check if the value (a * -1)  is present in the list. If (a * -1) is found, then the pair exists, but if we check all possible a values and do not find (a * -1) then there is no pair.

Q Text: You are given an unsorted list of positive and negative integers. You must determine if there exists a pair of values (a, b) such that a + b = 0. Which of the following approaches has the smallest (most efficient) time complexity? Assume that no index has the value 0.
Answer: Create a Hashset. Then, iterate through the list and for each value a check if (a * -1)  is in the Hashset. If it is, then the pair exists. If not, then add value a to the Hashset if it is not already present. If we check all possible a values without finding the pair then there is no pair.

Q Text: You are given an unsorted list of positive and negative integers. You must determine if there exists a pair of values (a, b) such that a + b = 0. Which of the following approaches has the smallest (most efficient) time complexity? Assume that no index has the value 0.
Answer: Sort the list. Then, iterate through the list and for each value a perform a binary search to check if the value (a * -1)  is present in the list. If (a * -1) is found, then the pair exists, but if we check all possible a values and do not find (a * -1) then there is no pair.

Q Text: You are given an unsorted list of positive and negative integers. You must determine if there exists a pair of values (a, b) such that a + b = 0. Which of the following approaches has the smallest (most efficient) time complexity? Assume that no index has the value 0.

If not, then add value a to the Hashset if it is not already present. If we check all possible a values without finding the pair then there is no pair.

Q Text: You are given an unsorted list of positive and negative integers. You must determine if there exists a pair of values (a, b) such that a + b = 0. Which of the following approaches has the smallest (most efficient) time complexity? Assume that no index has the value 0.
Answer: Create a Hashset. Then, iterate through the list and for each value a check if (a * -1)  is in the Hashset. If it is, then the pair exists. If not, then add value a to the Hashset if it is not already present. If we check all possible a values without finding the pair then there is no pair.

Q Text: You are given an unsorted list of positive and negative integers. You must determine if there exists a pair of values (a, b) such that a + b = 0. Which of the following approaches has the smallest (most efficient) time complexity? Assume that no index has the value 0.

Q Text: You are given an unsorted list of positive and negative integers. You must determine if there exists a pair of values (a, b) such that a + b = 0. Which of the following approaches has the smallest (most efficient) time complexity? Assume that no index has the value 0.
Answer: Sort the list. Then, iterate through the list and for each value a perform a binary search to check if the value (a * -1)  is present in the list. If (a * -1) is found, then the pair exists, but if we check all possible a values and do not find (a * -1) then there is no pair.

Q Text: You are given an unsorted list of positive and negative integers. You must determine if there exists a pair of values (a, b) such that a + b = 0. Which of the following approaches has the smallest (most efficient) time complexity? Assume that no index has the value 0.
Answer: Create a Hashset. Then, iterate through the list and for each value a check if (a * -1)  is in the Hashset. If it is, then the pair exists. If not, then add value a to the Hashset if it is not already present. If we check all possible a values without finding the pair then there is no pair.

Suppose you have n versions [1, 2, ..., n] and you want to find out the first bad one, which causes all the following ones to be bad. You can assume there will be at least 1 version.

Constraints:

1 <= bad <= n <= 231 - 1

Input: n = 5, bad = 4
Output: 4

call isBadVersion(3) -> false

call isBadVersion(4) -> true

# The isBadVersion API is already defined for you.
# @param version, an integer
# @return a bool
# def isBadVersion(version):

class Solution(object):
    def firstBadVersion(self, n):
        """
        :type n: int
        :rtype: int
        """
        left = 0
        right = n - 1
        mid = (left + right) // 2
        fbl = 1
        fbr = n

        while fbl != fbr:
            if isBadVersion(mid + 1):
                fbl = mid + 1
                right = mid - 1
            else:
                left = mid + 1
                fbr = mid + 2
            mid = (left + right) // 2
        return fbl

Q Text: You are given an unsorted list of positive and negative integers. You must determine if there exists a pair of values (a, b) such that a + b = 0. Which of the following approaches has the smallest (most efficient) time complexity? Assume that no index has the value 0.
Answer: Create a Hashset. Then, iterate through the list and for each value a check if (a * -1)  is in the Hashset. If it is, then the pair exists. If not, then add value a to the Hashset if it is not already present. If we check all possible a values without finding the pair then there is no pair.

Q Text: You are given an unsorted list of positive and negative integers. You must determine if there exists a pair of values (a, b) such that a + b = 0. Which of the following approaches has the smallest (most efficient) time complexity? Assume that no index has the value 0.
Answer: Use a nested loop to compare all possible combinations of two indices. For each combination, if their values sum to 0 then the pair exists. If we check all combinations of indices without finding the pair, then there is no pair.

    def firstBadVersion(self, n: int) -> int:
        low = 1
        high = n

        bad = isBadVersion(1)
        while low <= high:
            mid = low + int((high-low)/2)
            if mid == 1 and bad:
                return 1
            #print (mid)

Q Text: You are given an unsorted list of positive and negative integers. You must determine if there exists a pair of values (a, b) such that a + b = 0. Which of the following approaches has the smallest (most efficient) time complexity? Assume that no index has the value 0.

Q Text: You are given an unsorted list of positive and negative integers. You must determine if there exists a pair of values (a, b) such that a + b = 0. Which of the following approaches has the smallest (most efficient) time complexity? Assume that no index has the value 0.
Answer: Sort the list. Then, iterate through the list and for each value a perform a binary search to check if the value (a * -1)  is present in the list. If (a * -1) is found, then the pair exists, but if we check all possible a values and do not find (a * -1) then there is no pair.

Q Text: You are given an unsorted list of positive and negative integers. You must determine if there exists a pair of values (a, b) such that a + b = 0. Which of the following approaches has the smallest (most efficient) time complexity? Assume that no index has the value 0.
Answer: Create a Hashset. Then, iterate through the list and for each value a check if (a * -1)  is in the Hashset. If it is, then the pair exists. If not, then add value a to the Hashset if it is not already present. If we check all possible a values without finding the pair then there is no pair.

Q Text: You are given an unsorted list of positive and negative integers. You must determine if there exists a pair of values (a, b) such that a + b = 0. Which of the following approaches has the smallest (most efficient) time complexity? Assume that no index has the value 0.
Answer: Use a nested loop to compare all possible combinations of two indices. For each combination, if their values sum to 0 then the pair exists. If we check all combinations of indices without finding the pair, then there is no pair.
